subject.title: feat: validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)

question: Should Crabbox core permanently own a `--require-artifact-schema` flag and its custom fail-closed JSON Schema subset, or should repositories continue validating evidence inside their run command?
rationale: Both approaches can enforce evidence quality, but choosing the core flag creates a long-lived CLI and schema-language compatibility commitment that code review cannot infer from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Sponsor the core gate
options.body: Approve the permanent flag and subset contract, then require the parser fix and real SSH-backed proof before merge.

options.title: Version or rename the dialect
options.body: Keep centralized validation but expose an explicitly Crabbox-specific or versioned schema dialect rather than implying broad JSON Schema compatibility.

options.title: Keep validation repository-owned
options.body: Close the PR and document how run scripts should validate their own evidence before command success.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core gate
recommendation.body: Approve the permanent flag and subset contract, then require the parser fix and real SSH-backed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision extends the required-artifact behavior this contributor appears to have introduced.
